physical.notes: The cabinet/coin door wiring diagram (PDF page 106) draws the Memory Protect Switch, N.O., from CPU board CN6 pin 12 (BLK-RED) to BLK ground. se.c's ram_w refuses writes to the protected RAM while public -3 is 1, and sega.vbs names the address swMemoryProtect; a closed coin door is public -3 at 1 and an open door 0. The Diagnostic Aids page: opening the Coin Door after a CMOS RAM failure 'will initiate a Factory Restore (Reset), by opening the Memory Protect Switch'.

Printed dedicated switch DS-6 (#6 VOLUME (RED BUTTON) (In Test: LEFT)), wired GRY-BLU to CN6-P8 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The cabinet wiring diagram draws it among the PORTALS™ SERVICE BUTTONS on the coin door.

Printed dedicated switch DS-7 (#7 SERV. CRED. (GREEN BUTTON) (In Test: RIGHT)), wired GRY-VIO to CN6-P9 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The cabinet wiring diagram draws it among the PORTALS™ SERVICE BUTTONS on the coin door.

Printed dedicated switch DS-8 (#8 BEGIN TEST (BLACK BUTTON) (In Test: ENTER)), wired GRY-BLK to CN6-P10 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. physical.notes: Printed switch-matrix drive column 2, return row 6. The grid prints "4-BALL TROUGH VUK OPTO" with mounting class "Under P/F"; the page-15 switch table gives part "BOT TRANS: 520-5173-00 / BOT REC: 520-5174-00". The page-15 note: 'Sw. 14 / Sw. 15 have both REC/TRANS on 1 board respectively'; the board table names the Dual OPTO boards 515-0173-00 and 515-0174-00 '4-Ball Trough over Up-Kicker'. Whitestar's switch_r hands the CPU ~core_getSwCol and the driver's invSw is zero, so public 1 is the CPU's closed-contact reading. The Trough Up-Kicker Dual OPTO boards theory (PDF page 107) states the construction: with light on the receiver its output transistor is off and acts as an open switch; when the beam is blocked it conducts and acts as a closed switch, so the contact rests open. Retained table script: bsTrough.InitSw 0, 14, 13, 12, 11 (lines 156-159): 14 is the exit position the trough up-kicker empties, held at 1 while a ball waits there. The script also sets vpmNudge.TiltSwitch=14 (line 152), so the table's nudge tilt writes this trough opto instead of the plumb-bob tilt 56; both pinned corpus scripts of the later table set vpmNudge.TiltSwitch=56. Placement from the retained table's Kicker BallRelease (projection: cvpmBallStack bsTrough (InitSw 0, 14, 13, 12, 11) has no switch objects; projected onto its release kicker BallRelease).

The grid prints "4-BALL STACKING OPTO" with mounting class "Under P/F"; the page-15 switch table gives part "TOP TRANS: 520-5173-00 / TOP REC: 520-5174-00". The page-15 note: 'Sw. 14 / Sw. 15 have both REC/TRANS on 1 board respectively'; the board table names the Dual OPTO boards 515-0173-00 and 515-0174-00 '4-Ball Trough over Up-Kicker'. Whitestar's switch_r hands the CPU ~core_getSwCol and the driver's invSw is zero, so public 1 is the CPU's closed-contact reading. The Trough Up-Kicker Dual OPTO boards theory (PDF page 107) states the construction: with light on the receiver its output transistor is off and acts as an open switch; when the beam is blocked it conducts and acts as a closed switch, so the contact rests open. physical.notes: Printed dedicated switch DS-4 (#4 RIGHT FLIPPER E.O.S. (End-of-Stroke)), wired GRY-YEL to CN6-P6 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The grid prints its location 'in Cabinet side' like the flipper buttons; the 2-Flipper Circuit Wiring Diagram (PDF page 104) draws it 'ON ASSY.' as an N.C. switch, and the right Flipper Assembly (500-6307-00) lists the Power (End of Stroke) Switch 180-5149-00. The diagram explains that the switch opens about 1/16" when the flipper is energized and that the CPU applies another 40 ms pulse when it sees the switch close during a hold, because a shot forced the bat back. normally_closed is that construction: at rest the contact is closed (public 1) and it opens (public 0) at the end of the stroke. The driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) | FLIP_SOL(FLIP_L) without FLIP_EOS, so core_updateSw never writes this bit and the ROM reads whatever the host writes; a recreation that leaves it at 0 only loses the re-pulse. The retained script never writes it; sega.vbs names this address swURFlip/swULFlip, an upper-flipper label it writes only when an upper flipper solenoid is registered, which this table does not do. Placement from the retained table's Flipper RightFlipper (projection: the end-of-stroke contact sits on the flipper assembly; projected onto the flipper the table animates).

dedswitch_r routes the flipper column's upper-flipper button bit to U206 input 5 (DS-5). The dedicated-switch column prints '#5 NOT USED' in a black cell (GRY-GRN, CN6-P7), and the 2-Flipper Circuit Wiring Diagram draws 'UPPER LT or RT FLIPPER IN CABINET DEDICATED SWITCH DS-5' in green with a NOT USED tag. The ROM's own wiring table agrees: in the dedicated-switch-test harness run, harl_a40's Portals Dedicated Switch Test printed '#5 NOT USED / CN6-7 GRY-GRN CN6-1 BLK' while 88 was held, where the flipper-button controls printed '#1 LEFT FLIPPER BUTTON / CN6-2 GRY-BRN CN6-1 BLK' (84) and '#3 RIGHT FLIPPER BUTTON / CN6-4 GRY-ORG CN6-1 BLK' (82). Only the cabinet wiring diagram disagrees: it draws an 'UPPER RIGHT FLIPPER BUTTON' on GRY-GRN, CN6 pin 7, its label and wire in red, the colour the page also uses for the Start and Launch buttons and lamp 47. mechanisms.behavior: Four balls (the manual's front page: 'FOUR (4) PINBALLS MUST BE INSTALLED!') rest in the Ball Trough Assembly on micro switches 11 (left), 12 and 13 and on the VUK opto 14 at the up-kicker; the two Dual OPTO board pairs carry 14 at the bottom and the stacking opto 15 at the top. Q1 (26-1200) kicks the ball on 14 up past 15 into the shooter lane, and the rest roll one place toward the up-kicker. Hold each occupied position at 1 and pass the kicked ball through 15 as a short 1 pulse (beam blocked). In the gameplay runs the ROM fired Q1 on Start and after the drain. The retained table's bsTrough never writes 15.
mechanisms.label: 4-ball trough with up-kicker and stacking opto

mechanisms.behavior: A served ball comes to rest on shooter-lane switch 16, and Q2 (24-940, Ball Auto Launch Assembly with plunger assembly 515-5000-02) fires it up the lane. The cabinet wiring diagram names the cabinet's button 53 the LAUNCH (FIRE) BUTTON, but in the harness runs the ROM launched without it and a press changed nothing. The ROM fired Q2 40 ms after the ball reached 16 and, while the ball stayed, again 2.3 s later and eight more times about 0.5 s apart before giving up, which is the Operator Alert behaviour the manual's Diagnostic Aids page describes. The retained table holds the ball in the saucer Kicker2 until Q2 fires.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: The Lift (Motor) Assembly 500-6396-00-67 turns a cam (Lift Cam Assembly 515-7021-00) with an Autotrol 24 V AC motor (041-5072-02) that the Relay PC Board 520-5010-00 switches from Q19; the Lift Plate & Cycle Assembly 500-6362-01-67 carries the H-D FLSTF Fat Boy 1:10 motorcycle model and raises it in a 'wheelie' together with the kick-out trough. Micro switch 35 closes at the top of the cam (UP) and 36 at the bottom (DOWN). Q19 only runs the motor; the ROM stops it when the wanted position switch closes, so the direction comes from the cam, not from the controller. The manual's Motorcycle Test loads the trough only with the motorcycle UP and states that it returns DOWN on a game reset. In the harness runs with built-in mechanisms off, the ROM ran Q19 at power-up until 36 closed (with 35 closed at boot as well as with neither closed; with 36 closed at boot it never ran), and when the served ball reached the shooter lane it ran Q19 until 35 closed; 35 alone did not stop the power-up search, and the ball search ran Q19 through any position change. Technical Brief 49 adds a 68 Ω adapter harness for motors that stutter on 50 Hz mains. The retained table models the lift as a one-solenoid reversing cvpmMech of 25 steps with 35 at the end step and 36 at step 0, and tilts its motorcycle primitives with it.
mechanisms.label: Motorcycle lift

positions.description: Motorcycle raised; the kick-out trough can take balls.
positions.label: Up

positions.description: Motorcycle lowered; the home position after power-up and a game reset.
positions.label: Down

mechanisms.behavior: The Kick-Out Trough Assembly 500-6397-00 rides under the motorcycle: a sloped trough over one 4-position membrane switch 181-5001-00, 44 at the bottom (the first ball in) to 41 at the top (the fourth), with its diodes on the Diode PC Board 520-5146-00, and the Q5 24-940 coil at its low end. The motorcycle-enter opto 37 (Long-Hop boards on the Stop Light Assembly's bracket) sees a ball entering. The Motorcycle Test loads balls by hand with the motorcycle UP and ejects them with Q5 from the Launch button. PinMAME's simulator for this game lets a ball into the trough only when the lift is at least half up and otherwise returns it to the playfield. In the gameplay runs a ball held on 44 for 10 s drew the trough up-kicker Q1 (a new ball), the shaker and flashers 29 and 30, and switched off the motor relay Q19 that had been running, but drew no Q5; no run fired Q5. The retained table stacks balls entering Kicker1 in bsCycle and ejects them on Q5 whatever the lift's position.
mechanisms.label: Motorcycle kick-out trough

mechanisms.behavior: The Ball Under-Trough Assembly 500-6401-00 carries a micro switch (48, 'Behind Top VUK (Metal Under-Trough)') and leads the ball to the Super VUK Assembly 500-6184-05, where it rests on micro switch 45 until Q3 (23-800) kicks it up. In the gameplay runs a ball held on 45 drew repeated Q3 kicks; a closure of 48 fired no coil and started the ROM's video mode, with the G.I. off. PinMAME's simulator routes a ball the magnet catches behind the traffic light to 48 and on to 45. The retained table kicks the ball out of sw45a.
mechanisms.label: Super VUK and under-trough

mechanisms.behavior: The Kick-Big (Power Scoop) Assembly 500-6398-00 below the bumpers: a ball resting on micro switch 46 is kicked out by Q4 (23-800) through the Power Scoop Weldment 515-6022-00. In the launch-scoop-opto run a ball held on 46 drew three flashes of the scoop flasher 20 and the first Q4 kick about 1.1 s after it arrived, then one every 0.75 s, ten in all, while it stayed.
mechanisms.label: Power scoop (Kick Big)

PinMAME publishes Q15 at 47/48 and Q16 at 45/46.

physical.notes: Coils Detailed Chart Table (DR. 6) row #19 "MOTOR RELAY": drive transistor Q19, cell "Relay Bd. / 520-5010-00". Q19 drives the Relay PC Board 520-5010-00, whose contact runs the lift motor: the Lift (Motor) Assembly 500-6396-00-67 carries the Motor & Connector Assembly 515-7025-00-67 (motor 'Autotrol 20 RPM 24v AC CCW' 041-5072-02 with a capacitor and a neon bulb), the Lift Cam Assembly 515-7021-00 and the position switches 35 and 36. Technical Brief 49 (October 21, 1999) adds a 50Hz Interface Harness 036-5425-01 with a 68 Ω 2 W resistor between the motor and game harness connectors, because some motors stuttered on 50 Hz mains. physical.notes: One G.I. relay on the I-O Power Driver Board 520-5137-01 (U206 74HCT273 data latch output D0 through R254 1K and the Q200 2N3904 relay driver, coil on 20v DC with D229 1N4004 across it) switches the 6.3v AC G.I. supply from J14 to the four separately fused circuits on J15 (General Illumination Circuit Detailed Wiring Diagram, PDF page 101): B, F24, BRN-WHT to WHT-BRN, Upper Left Playfield, 10 #44; Y, F25, YEL to WHT-YEL, Upr. Rt. & Lwr. Right P/F, 10 #44; G, F26, GRN to WHT-GRN, Lower Left P/F + Coin Door, 8 #44 plus 2 #555 on the coin door; V, F27, VIO to WHT-VIO, Upper Right Playfield, 10 #44. The page warns that G.I. bulb quantities may change during production; its bottom-of-playfield drawing marks 38 circuit-lettered sockets. The quantity 40 is those 38 playfield bulbs plus the two coin-door bulbs. se.c publishes the relay as GI 0, and the harness runs saw it on in attract mode, blink with each coin, the right ramp exit (26) and the outlanes (57, 60), and switch off during the video mode the Behind Top VUK switch (48) starts. The retained table does not bind GI 0 (UseGI = 0, line 9; its PFGI sub, lines 107-117, is bound to no callback), so its GI collection stays lit. That collection holds the 20 Lights GI_001 to GI_020, each a single socket; each is placed, observed only, as a playfield bulb. They are 20 of the 38 playfield sockets; the drawing's circuit letters have not been matched to them, so no placement carries a string, and the other 18 and the two coin-door bulbs are counted but not placed.
